applied.quote: According to [IRS rules for deducting expenses](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/deducting-business-expenses), capital equipment like cameras, computers, and lighting setups must be depreciated across multiple tax years following Publication 946 and reported on Form 4562.
applied.replacement: According to [IRS rules for deducting expenses](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/deducting-business-expenses), equipment depreciation is handled following Publication 946 and reported on Form 4562.
applied.why: SOURCE does not name cameras, computers, or lighting setups.

applied.quote: Monthly subscriptions for video editing tools, music libraries, and software used to manage channel content qualify as current operational deductions.
applied.replacement: Monthly subscriptions for video editing tools and software used to manage channel content qualify as current operational deductions.

applied.quote: Creators tracking actual utility, insurance, and housing expenses instead calculate their deduction on Form 8829.

applied.quote: Deducting camera gear and computers used for personal tasks without separating and excluding the non-business percentage.

applied.quote: Google issues Form 1099-MISC, Form 1099-K, or Form 1042-S depending on the account classification and payment method.

applied.why: SOURCE does not state what determines which form Google issues.

applied.quote: Creators operating as a business can deduct ordinary and necessary expenses, including video editing tools, music licensing, software subscriptions, and production equipment depreciated under IRS rules.
applied.replacement: Creators operating as a business can deduct ordinary and necessary expenses, including video editing tools, software subscriptions, and equipment depreciated under IRS rules.

applied.quote: You can also claim a qualifying home studio used regularly and exclusively for channel production.
applied.replacement: You can also claim a qualifying home office used regularly and exclusively for channel production.
applied.why: SOURCE refers to a home office, not a home studio.

applied.quote: If the IRS classifies your channel as a hobby, you report gross revenue on Schedule 1 without standard business expense deductions.
applied.replacement: If the IRS classifies your channel as a hobby, you report gross revenue on Schedule 1.

applied.quote: You must check your specific statement in your Google account dashboard rather than assuming a single form type.

applied.why: SOURCE does not mention 'dashboard'; it instructs to check the form actually received.

applied.quote: Google's documentation does not specify which form each creator receives, so check the tax documents section inside your account.
applied.replacement: Google's documentation does not specify which form each creator receives, so check the form you actually receive.
applied.why: SOURCE does not mention 'tax documents section inside your account'; only check yours.

applied.quote: YouTube earnings count as taxable income starting from the first dollar.
applied.replacement: [YouTube](https://blog.youtube/creator-and-artist-stories/youtube-partner-program-explained/) earnings count as taxable income starting from the first dollar.
applied.why: Links YouTube to its official partner program overview on first mention.

applied.quote: If you run your channel with regular continuity to turn a profit, the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) classifies the income as self-employment earnings once your net profit hits $400 for the tax year.
applied.replacement: If you run your channel regularly to make a profit, it counts as a business. You then owe self-employment tax once net earnings reach $400 for the year, [according to the Internal Revenue Service (IRS)](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/self-employment-tax-social-security-and-medicare-taxes).
applied.type: Y-2 misstated threshold and unlinked IRS
applied.why: Clarifies business classification and links IRS guidance on the $400 self-employment tax threshold.

applied.quote: That classification means you owe self-employment tax alongside standard federal income tax, though ordinary equipment, editing software, and subscription costs reduce your taxable base.
applied.replacement: You also owe federal income tax on the profit, and ordinary and necessary costs such as equipment, editing software and subscriptions reduce it.
applied.type: Y-2 backward phrasing and missing necessary rule
applied.why: Replaces backward phrasing and includes ordinary and necessary requirement for deductible expenses.

applied.quote: The [self-employment tax rate](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/self-employment-tax-social-security-and-medicare-taxes) is 15.3%
applied.replacement: The self-employment tax rate is 15.3%
applied.why: Removes duplicate link to ensure first-mention-only rule is satisfied.

applied.quote: examiners review multiple factors to decide if an activity qualifies as a business
applied.replacement: the IRS lists factors that help decide whether an activity is a business
applied.why: Source states IRS lists factors rather than mentioning examiners specifically.

applied.quote: its primary objective is income
applied.replacement: its primary purpose is income or profit
applied.type: Y-3 phrasing mismatch with Schedule C instructions
applied.why: Matches exact Schedule C wording for trade or business qualification.

applied.quote: If your earnings pass $200,000 for single filers or $250,000 for married couples filing jointly, an Additional Medicare Tax of 0.9% applies.
applied.replacement: An Additional Medicare Tax of 0.9% applies to earnings above $200,000 for single filers or $250,000 for married couples filing jointly.
applied.why: Clarifies that the 0.9% tax applies only to earnings above the statutory thresholds.

applied.quote: Collecting your earnings requires submitting your tax information directly to Google.
applied.replacement: [Google](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/10391362?hl=en) must collect tax information from creators in the YouTube Partner Program.

applied.replacement: Google does not withhold

applied.why: Removes duplicate link and attribution following revised preceding sentence.

applied.quote: Non-US creators who submit a Form W-8 face withholding between 0% and 30% on earnings from US viewers based on applicable tax treaties, while non-US accounts without tax info default to 30% withholding on US earnings.
applied.replacement: Non-US creators who submit a Form W-8 face withholding of 0% to 30% on earnings from US viewers, depending on tax-treaty status. Non-US business accounts without tax info default to 30% of US earnings.

applied.why: Splits long sentence and clarifies 30% withholding applies to non-US business accounts.

applied.quote: [Google reports year-end earnings](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/10390801?hl=en) using Form 1099-MISC, Form 1099-K, or Form 1042-S, but its documentation does not specify which form applies to each creator profile.
applied.replacement: [Google's YouTube help](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/10390801?hl=en) lists Form 1099-MISC, Form 1099-K and Form 1042-S as year-end forms, but it does not say which form applies to which creator.
applied.why: Source only lists forms without confirming Google reports using all of them.

applied.quote: Tax reporting rules also depend on information return minimums.

applied.why: Reflects that the $2,000 minimum applies to rents and other income boxes.

applied.quote: by paying either 90% of your current tax year liability or 100% of your prior-year tax

applied.quote: Yes, you must file a tax return.

applied.quote: If the IRS classifies your channel as a hobby, you report gross revenue on Schedule 1.
applied.replacement: If the IRS treats your channel as a hobby, you report the income on Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 8.
applied.why: Avoids implying gross revenue deduction rules by naming Schedule 1 line 8 directly.

applied.quote: If you produce videos for a [faceless YouTube channel with AI](/guides/faceless-youtube-channel-ai/), monthly generator access fees directly support production and count as business expenses.
